candidates.next_evidence: Review latest 10-K/10-Q segment disclosures, cloud subscription growth, services backlog, customer go-lives, partner ecosystem disclosures, Gartner/IDC positioning, and any disclosed large retailer implementations.

candidates.why_include: Its 2025 10-K describes software for supply chains, inventory, and omnichannel operations for retailers and other organizations, including enterprise inventory availability, order fulfillment optimization, WMS, TMS, and cloud subscription revenue tied to Manhattan Active omnichannel, warehouse, and transportation products.

candidates.next_evidence: Check 2025 10-K and 2026 quarterly filings for recurring revenue growth, net customer adds, average recurring revenue per customer, retailer network expansion, churn, implementation capacity, and acquisition integration.

candidates.why_underfollowed: More likely classified as logistics software or trade-compliance software than consumer retail infrastructure, even though the need for faster delivery, carrier orchestration, and cross-border ecommerce execution is directly tied to consumer demand.

evidence.claim: Manhattan Associates develops, sells, deploys, services, and maintains software solutions for supply chains, inventory, and omnichannel operations for retailers, wholesalers, manufacturers, logistics providers, and other organizations; its filings describe order management, store inventory and fulfillment, WMS, TMS, enterprise inventory, and cloud subscription revenue tied to Manhattan Active omnichannel, warehouse, and transportation products.

SPS Commerce describes itself as a cloud-based retail supply-chain management provider connecting retailers, grocers, distributors, suppliers, manufacturers, and logistics firms, with network effects and products for collaboration, order visibility, inventory management, and trading-partner relationships.

SPS Commerce's 2025 filing states that retailers need automation as store openings/closings, labor shortages, supply-chain disruptions, and new buying patterns require retailers and trading partners to become more agile.

Descartes' annual materials describe cloud logistics technology, ecommerce growth, logistics management technology, collaboration with trading partners, and modules including routing, mobile, telematics, ecommerce, shipping, and fulfillment.
evidence.source_title: The Descartes Systems Group 2025 Annual Materials

evidence.claim: Descartes announced the acquisition of OrderMine, described as an AI-powered forecasting and demand-planning provider designed to support ecommerce businesses across their growth lifecycle.
evidence.source_title: The Descartes Systems Group Fiscal 2026 Annual Report Exhibit

evidence.claim: Zebra provides barcode scanners, RFID readers, mobile computers, printers, real-time locating systems, UWB-related supplies and services, rugged mobile devices, scanners, and software.

Zebra's data-capture and asset-visibility products are plausible infrastructure inputs for omnichannel order orchestration because OMS/WMS/WES systems require accurate inventory, location, pick, pack, and ship-event data from stores and warehouses.

E2open was a relevant public candidate for cloud-based end-to-end omnichannel and supply-chain management software, but it appears to have been delisted after acquisition by WiseTech Global, so it is not retained in the US-listed candidate universe.
evidence.source_title: E2open Market Capitalization and Delisting Note

memory_update.text: MANH is the reference benchmark for omnichannel order management, warehouse management, WES, TMS, and retail fulfillment orchestration; useful for validating product taxonomy and customer workflow relevance.

SPSC is an underfollowed consumer-retail supply-chain network candidate: less obvious than OMS/WMS vendors but exposed to retailer-supplier onboarding, EDI, product/order visibility, and trading-partner automation.

DSGX is an underfollowed second-order ecommerce fulfillment and logistics execution candidate through ecommerce shipping, routing, mobile, telematics, trade compliance, carrier connectivity, and logistics-network data.

ZBRA should be tracked as a physical data-capture infrastructure supplier for omnichannel execution, not as a pure software vendor; evidence needs retail/ecommerce end-market growth, RFID adoption, and software attach-rate confirmation.

E2open fits the node conceptually but appears no longer suitable for the US-listed universe after WiseTech acquisition/delisting; consider WiseTech only if non-US listings are allowed in a later pass.

node: Omnichannel order management, warehouse execution, and fulfillment orchestration software
summary: Expanded the universe around scarce, deeply embedded omnichannel and fulfillment-execution software. The cleanest reference name is Manhattan Associates, but the underfollowed lane includes SPS Commerce and Descartes, which sit one step away from obvious consumer retail demand through retail trading networks, logistics execution, ecommerce shipping, routing, and fulfillment data flows. Zebra is included as a second-order infrastructure provider because order orchestration systems depend on frontline barcode/RFID/mobile-computing data capture in stores, warehouses, yards, and delivery workflows. E2open was considered but is flagged as a coverage gap rather than a candidate because it appears to have been acquired/delisted in 2025.
